analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump (line 3) and a rewrite of the forced tool_choice paragraph near base lines 2017-2019. The supplied base text covers the surrounding sections. The head text is visible only through the patch.

New documentation claims: the coordinator routes required/named tool_choice requests only to builds listed in `tool_constraint_models`. `ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability` fills that list per exact build. A table adds Qwen3.5-9B, qwen3.5-35b-a3b, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8 and mimo-v2.6-flash-mopd, each tied to its own model_type. Forced calls are prompt-forced, withheld and schema-validated (`.structuredPostValidation`). In forced mode `NativeToolStreamRouter` drops ASCII framing whitespace around call frames. Whitespace alone counts as a missing call. Any other visible text is a 422 `tool_choice` violation.

No code, config or control changed, so there is no direct regression against T-041, TB-002, TB-007 or the other retained threats. The claims are consistent with the existing model-blind, validate-before-release design. The text does not weaken schema validation, the encrypted prefix-cache posture (T-041) or the coordinator-to-provider contract.

I cannot verify that the described implementation matches the source. The source files are `ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift`, `NativeToolStreamRouter` and `ToolConstraintValidation`, and none were supplied. The same applies to whether the coordinator actually gates routing on `tool_constraint_models`. This is a documentation-accuracy question for the PR's code-side companion, not evidence of a vulnerability here. I found no new attack surface and nothing that invalidates a threat-model assumption in this diff.
